gloss: to lay bare; to expose; to reveal

definitions.gloss: to lay bare; to expose; to reveal openly
definitions.explanation: To expose something (often something normally hidden) for all to see. Used both literally for physical exposure and figuratively for revealing emotions, secrets, or true nature.

examples.japanese: {本性|ほんしょう}を{晒|さら}け{出|だ}した。
{彼女|かのじょ}は{感情|かんじょう}を{晒|さら}け{出|だ}すのが{苦手|にがて}だ。
examples.english: She has difficulty laying her emotions bare.

examples.japanese: あの{政治家|せいじか}は{不正|ふせい}を{晒|さら}け{出|だ}されて{辞任|じにん}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれた。
examples.english: That politician was forced to resign after his corruption was exposed.

notes:
A godan verb combining {晒|さら}す (to expose) with {出|だ}す (to put out). Carries a stronger nuance than simply "showing" — it implies baring something that is normally concealed or private. The passive form {晒|さら}け{出|だ}される is common when someone's secrets or misdeeds are involuntarily revealed.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {本性|ほんしょう}を{晒|さら}け{出|だ}す — to reveal one's true nature
- {感情|かんじょう}を{晒|さら}け{出|だ}す — to lay one's emotions bare
- {弱|よわ}さを{晒|さら}け{出|だ}す — to expose one's weakness
- {全|すべ}てを{晒|さら}け{出|だ}す — to lay everything bare

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {暴|あば}く — to expose/uncover (often used for exposing crimes or secrets; more forceful)
- {曝|さら}す — to expose (to elements or danger; different nuance from emotional revelation)
- {明|あ}かす — to reveal/disclose (more neutral; simply making something known)
